title: Rich textual-data sources review: the catalogue of 25 source families
scope: Representative review of provider documentation and metadata. No source datasets acquired, proposed tasks executed or study fit validated.

families.name: Amazon Reviews 2023
families.release: 2023 release; creator Hugging Face metadata revision 2b6d039ed471f2ba5fd2acb718bf33b0a7e5598e (modified 2024-12-08). This pins the repository metadata, not every externally hosted category file.
families.units_and_scope: User–item reviews and product metadata, across Amazon categories.
families.size: Creator reports 571.54 million reviews, 54.51 million users and 48.19 million items; metadata coverage is not identical to reviewed-item coverage.
families.coverage_and_dates: Review dates May 1996–September 2023. Product metadata is a snapshot, not a historical price or product-attribute panel.
families.fields_and_links: Review text/title, rating, user_id, timestamps, verified purchase, helpful votes and images; item title, descriptions, features, categories, store and price. Join reviews to metadata with parent_asin; do not silently reuse older ASIN join assumptions.
families.access: public-download; reuse unclear
families.route: Creator category JSON downloads and Hugging Face repository.
families.authentication: Creator links and HF metadata are public; HF gated=false. File acquisition was not tested.
families.inspected: Primary documentation and native HF metadata inspected. Do not execute the custom HF loader; use native data files in a later acquisition.
families.reuse_terms: No explicit dataset license found on the inspected creator site or HF metadata. Public availability does not establish permission to redistribute review text or images.
limitations: Ratings and helpful votes are reception measures, not novelty labels or an unbiased quality standard.
Items are not firms; review selection and product survival can distort organizational inferences.
Actual files need schema inspection: documentation and examples vary in timestamp/helpful-vote naming and price type. User identifiers and review text need a deliberate sharing plan.
families.suggested_task: Separate claims about product attributes from customer experience and unsupported inferences; compare conventional text features with constrained LLM extraction.
families.review_decision: Rich review and product measurement material, conditional on clear reuse terms and a frozen native partition.

documentation.label: Hou et al., 2024, Bridging Language and Items

families.name: Google Local Data 2021
families.release: US Google Local 2021 collection, through September 2021; no per-file checksum manifest inspected.
families.units_and_scope: Dated reviews of local businesses, business responses, and business metadata.
families.size: 666,324,103 reviews; 113,643,107 users; 4,963,111 businesses. Vermont partition: 852,203 reviews and 11,291 businesses.
families.coverage_and_dates: Review time and response time are available. Business attributes are snapshot values; collection coverage is not an operating-history panel.
families.fields_and_links: Review user_id, time, rating, text, pictures, resp.time and resp.text; business gmap_id, name, address, categories, coordinates, hours, price and related-business identifiers. Join on gmap_id.
families.access: public-download; reuse unclear
families.route: Creator per-state metadata/reviews, 10-core subsets and ratings-only links.
families.authentication: No authentication stated for direct links; no data downloaded.
families.inspected: Creator data format, files and citation inspected.
families.reuse_terms: No explicit dataset reuse license found on the dataset-specific page. Do not infer an open license from UCSD hosting.
limitations: Ratings-only files cannot support the proposed text task; 10-core filtering changes the target population.
A response does not establish that remediation occurred, and a related-business link does not establish common ownership.
Even a state partition is large. Business names and user information should not be copied into a public sample without checking permitted reuse.
families.suggested_task: Construct evidence-linked complaint, promised action and response-lag observations, explicitly retaining missing responses.
families.review_decision: Strong candidate for observable review–response episodes; reuse terms and partition acquisition remain unresolved.

families.name: Food.com Recipes and User Interactions
families.release: Creator Kaggle dataset version 2, updated 2019-11-08T01:18:21.147Z; native metadata inspected.
families.units_and_scope: Recipes and user–recipe interactions from the 2000–2018 collection.
families.size: 231,637 recipes, 226,570 users and 1,132,367 reviews in the UCSD directory; Kaggle package metadata reports 280,350,373 bytes. The paper's filtered analysis sample is smaller.
families.coverage_and_dates: Recipe submitted dates and interaction dates allow a declared temporal reference set; exact date completeness remains untested.
families.fields_and_links: Recipes: id, name, contributor_id, submitted, ingredients, steps, tags, nutrition, minutes and counts. Interactions: user_id, recipe_id, date, rating and review. Link recipe_id to recipe id.
families.access: public listing; download authentication unverified; reuse restricted/unclear
families.route: Original shuyangli94 Kaggle listing; do not substitute a similarly named scrape.
families.authentication: Kaggle download may require an account; no download or login was attempted.
families.inspected: Creator directory, paper, and native Kaggle metadata match this dataset identity.
families.reuse_status: copyright notice; no broad reuse grant found
families.reuse_terms: Creator metadata says “Data files © Original Authors.” A different Food.com scrape's CC0 label cannot license this release.
limitations: Ratings measure reception, not novelty; nutrition fields do not by themselves validate health claims.
The paper applies recipe/user filtering and chronological splits: do not treat its filtered counts as the raw package.
Recipe posting dates indicate publication in this source, not invention dates.
families.suggested_task: Compare ingredient-pair rarity, text distance and blinded judgments of substantive change. Use recipes with similar prose but different composition and the converse.
families.review_decision: Interpretable recipe-recombination demonstration, conditional on reuse and acquisition.

families.name: RecipePairs / SHARE recipe-editing data
families.release: Creator HF revision fb87cbf30db41c4214e647a6bfac2f1dcb862c3e, modified 2023-03-21; card configuration 1.5.0.
families.units_and_scope: Derived pairs of recipes and a linked recipe-content table. The original SHARE study's selected benchmark is a different manifestation.
families.size: HF card reports 6,908,697 pair examples; pairs.parquet 71,788,476 bytes and recipes.parquet 169,885,896 bytes. The 2022 paper describes about 83K pairs. Selection/release reconciliation is unresolved.
families.coverage_and_dates: Pair-table dates were not verified; historical novelty requires a checked join to original recipe dates.
families.fields_and_links: Recipe-pair identifiers, similarity and dietary tags; linked recipe content in the separate recipes table. Exact parquet schema and key uniqueness require later inspection.
families.access: public-download; declared GPL-3.0 with upstream-rights caveat
families.route: Creator HF native parquet files.
families.authentication: gated=false in creator metadata; no file acquisition.
families.inspected: Creator card, repository file metadata and primary SHARE paper inspected.
families.reuse_terms: HF labels this dataset GPL-3.0. That declaration does not settle rights in the underlying Food.com content or prove the paper's selected benchmark has identical terms.
limitations: Pairs are derived/matched examples, not observed human creative lineage, editing decisions or accepted improvements.
The roughly 83K-paper versus 6.9M-card discrepancy must be resolved before numerical replication.
Dataset-license labeling alone does not resolve underlying source rights.
families.suggested_task: Compare lexical distance with changes to ingredients and procedural dependencies. Treat dietary labels as constraints to inspect rather than certified nutritional advice.
families.review_decision: Diagnostic complement to Food.com; resolve the mismatch between the hosted dataset and published benchmark before acquisition.

families.name: Goodreads / UCSD Book Graph
families.release: Late-2017 collection with May-2019 revisions documented on the moved-from UCSD Book Graph site. Current acquisition link not verified.
families.units_and_scope: Books, works, authors, series, public user interactions and reviews.
families.size: Creator page reports 2,360,655 books, 1,521,962 works, 829,529 authors, 400,390 series and 876,145 users; revised interactions 229,154,523 and approximately 15.7M reviews. Older counts on the same page describe earlier versions.
families.coverage_and_dates: Public interaction/review dates where present; edition publication and work identity require separate treatment.
families.fields_and_links: Book/user/review IDs; book-to-work, author and series links; shelves, reading/rating actions, text reviews and dates. Genre subsets can overlap.
families.access: academic-use-only; current download unverified
families.route: Creator site moved from the UCSD Google Site to mengtingwan.github.io; old Drive paths are deprecated.
families.authentication: Current download and any account requirement not verified.
families.inspected: Detailed moved-from creator documentation inspected; current page did not render substantive content in the text browser.
families.reuse_terms: Creator terms limit use to academic research, prohibit redistribution and prohibit commercial use. Do not bundle source reviews in a portable sample.
limitations: Similar-book graphs may not be closed within a genre subset.
Reading/rating activity and panel agreement do not measure durable evaluative skill.
Terms and current download availability make this a less portable starter than explicitly licensed sources.
families.suggested_task: Compare description-level similarity with audience interpretation while keeping author, work and edition units separate.
families.review_decision: Cultural-data reserve with explicit restrictions; verify the current creator route before acquisition.

families.name: MovieLens 32M
families.release: Stable ml-32m generated 2023-10-13; per-file MD5 values in the README.
families.units_and_scope: Movie ratings and tag applications by users with at least twenty ratings; movie identity links.
families.size: 32,000,204 ratings; 2,000,072 tag applications; 87,585 movies; 200,948 users.
families.coverage_and_dates: Ratings from 1995-01-09 through 2023-10-12; ratings and tags carry timestamps.
families.fields_and_links: movies(movieId,title,genres), ratings(userId,movieId,rating,timestamp), tags(userId,movieId,tag,timestamp), links(movieId,imdbId,tmdbId). No demographics or full review corpus.
families.access: public-download; custom research terms
families.route: GroupLens static ZIP and README.
families.authentication: No login documented for download; no ZIP acquired.
families.inspected: Official release and full README inspected.
families.reuse_terms: Acknowledge GroupLens; redistribution/transformation must retain the applicable conditions; commercial or revenue-bearing use requires permission. This is not an unrestricted open-data license.
limitations: The at-least-twenty-ratings inclusion criterion selects active users.
Cross-site IDs do not grant rights to external film content.
A dated rating records a platform action rather than initial exposure or a selection decision.
families.suggested_task: Build a transparent linkage demonstration and compare summary ratings with selected content measures.
families.review_decision: Structured comparison material; weaker as the main organizational-text demonstration.

families.name: Open Food Facts
families.release: Continuously updated product database; documentation checked 2026-10-11. No dated data snapshot acquired or frozen. Current API documentation identifies v3.6, with v2 deprecated.
families.units_and_scope: Barcode-identified food products with contributed structured fields and label images.
families.size: No current exact product count verified; avoid quoting a moving website total.
families.coverage_and_dates: Record creation/modification timestamps concern database observations, not product launch dates or invention.
families.fields_and_links: Barcode/code joins product names, brands, categories, ingredients, nutrients, labels and images. Brand names are not resolved firm identifiers.
families.access: public access; explicitly licensed database
families.route: Official API and documented bulk export route; bounded API retrieval would suit a later small demo.
families.authentication: Reads do not require authentication; official docs require a custom User-Agent. No data records acquired.
families.inspected: Official API and rights documentation inspected; the main data page did not render in the browser.
families.reuse_terms: Database: ODbL; individual database contents: DbCL; images: CC BY-SA. Preserve attribution and applicable share-alike obligations. Third-party label artwork/content can have additional rights; do not assume one license covers every component.
limitations: Crowdsourced coverage and field missingness can differ systematically by product/region.
Structured entries are comparison evidence, not infallible ground truth.
A product snapshot supports relative difference within the reference set; it cannot establish historical novelty or market introduction.
families.suggested_task: Create a new coded observation of a packaging or ingredient claim, linking each decision to the label source and checking against structured metadata.
families.review_decision: Starter choice for product measurement with explicit component licenses and lightweight access.

documentation.label: Field examples and API cheat sheet

families.name: USPTO PatentsView disambiguated patent data
families.release: Current USPTO description covers granted and pre-grant releases through 2025-12-31, with annualized derivative panels updated December 2025. Exact ODP file manifest/version was not obtained.
families.units_and_scope: Patents/applications with disambiguated inventor and assignee entities, technology classifications and citations.
families.size: Current row/file counts not verified. Coverage start depends on the selected table; do not transfer an old API count to the current bulk release.
families.coverage_and_dates: Application, publication and grant dates have different meanings. Historical reference sets must use information actually public before each target cutoff.
families.fields_and_links: Patent/application identifiers link bibliographic records, text tables, inventors, assignees, classifications and citations. Disambiguation versions can change longitudinal entity links.
families.access: registration-controlled public source; current release terms unresolved
families.route: USPTO Open Data Portal bulk datasets, including pvgpatdis; legacy PatentSearch is not assumed to be an available route.
families.authentication: ODP registration/API-key requirement announced effective 2026-06-18, with additional profile fields in August 2026. No account or key used.
families.inspected: Current USPTO source and ODP access notices inspected; current file acquisition untested.
families.reuse_terms: A legacy PatentSearch 2024 release explicitly states CC BY 4.0. Do not automatically transfer that statement to every current ODP file; check release-specific terms when acquiring.
limitations: Citations can reflect examiners and legal drafting as well as inventor knowledge search.
Grant timing cannot substitute for information availability; patents are selected inventions rather than the full innovation population.
Text metrics and citations do not reveal aspiration levels, internal search decisions or commercial value.
families.suggested_task: Compare technical-component recombination with lexical distance, then construct a small source-linked assignee entry/event table.
families.review_decision: Strong innovation candidate, conditional on current ODP access and release-manifest verification.

families.name: SEC EDGAR filings and company facts
families.release: Live submissions and XBRL APIs, updated in real time with nightly bulk packages. A dated source manifest must be frozen for a study; none was acquired here.
families.units_and_scope: Issuer filings, filing events and standardized financial facts; issuer is identified by CIK.
families.size: No finite study population selected. Submission responses include recent history and pointers to older chunks; do not infer full coverage from the initial response.
families.coverage_and_dates: Filing dates, reporting periods and event dates are distinct. XBRL required from 2009; amendments and restatements matter for as-of analyses.
families.fields_and_links: Ten-digit CIK, accession, form, dates and primary document link; names/tickers/exchanges; company facts keyed by taxonomy/concept/unit and filing context. Standardized aggregated facts omit custom tags.
families.access: public access with official dissemination permission
families.route: data.sec.gov submission/companyfacts endpoints and SEC filing documents.
families.authentication: No API key required; identify automated requests and respect the official aggregate limit of ten requests/second.
families.inspected: Official API and privacy/dissemination documentation inspected. No filing records acquired.
families.reuse_terms: SEC policy permits copying/distributing public information with source acknowledgment; logos/artwork have exclusions. Do not label every third-party exhibit public domain merely because EDGAR hosts it.
limitations: Filings are issuer representations and legally structured disclosures, not direct observation of internal decision processes.
Current facts and last-filed frames can leak later restatements into historical analyses.
A financial outcome is not an aspiration threshold, and a disclosure date is not necessarily a decision date.
families.suggested_task: Create NEW event-level observations: issuer, role, event type, interim status, event date, disclosure date, accession and supporting passage. Resolve duplication and distinguish absence from unreported detail.
families.review_decision: Starter choice for organizational disclosure research with stable identities and official source traces.

families.name: Federal Register documents and metadata
families.provider: Office of the Federal Register and Government Publishing Office
families.release: Continuously updated API; published documents from 1994, public-inspection documents from November 2011. Freeze a dated query, identifiers and official source versions for any new dataset.
families.units_and_scope: Regulatory/public-notice documents, their agency associations and separately coded obligations/events.
families.size: No fixed study count obtained. API pagination returns only the first 2,000 results; partition queries by dates rather than assuming that a single broad query is complete.
families.coverage_and_dates: Publication, effective, comment and action dates are different. Date presence and legal status need document-level checking.
families.fields_and_links: Document number, publication date, document type, issuing agencies, title and full-text/PDF references; docket/RIN links where present. Issuing agency is not automatically the implementing actor.
families.access: public access; government-content reuse with exclusions
families.route: Official JSON/CSV API and document pages; use the linked official PDF/govinfo text when legal wording matters.
families.authentication: No API key required; no records downloaded.
families.inspected: Official developer documentation and Library of Congress rights statement inspected.
families.reuse_terms: US government content is generally public domain; reprinted third-party copyrighted material can be an exception. NARA/OFR seals are not freely reusable. Do not blanket-license every attachment.
limitations: The measured outcome is an explicit textual obligation, not observed cooperation or successful implementation.
Corrections, multiple documents per rule and multiple obligations per document change denominators.
API XML is informational; official PDF references matter. Existing corpus ownership does not make the new coded dataset already built.
families.suggested_task: Construct NEW document–obligation records: implementing agency, assigned action, counterpart, authority, date, evidence passage and uncertainty. Distinguish issuing agencies, historical mentions, consultation and explicit implementation duties.
families.review_decision: Strong source for regulatory framing and stated obligations; a committee creation, renewal and termination table is one proposed demonstration.

families.name: OpenAlex scholarly graph
families.release: Live graph and public snapshot route; documentation checked 2026-10-11. No current snapshot manifest pinned.
families.units_and_scope: Works, authors, institutions and related scholarly entities linked through identifiers, authorship and citations.
families.size: Current exact graph size not verified; the 2022 paper's size is historical and is not a current release count.
families.coverage_and_dates: Publication dates and snapshot dates differ; entity resolution, affiliations and classifications can change.
families.fields_and_links: Work IDs/DOIs, titles, dates, authorship/institutions, references/citations and abstracts where available. Full article text is not guaranteed by metadata availability.
families.access: CC0 metadata; API account/key for regular use
families.route: Current API access documentation and public snapshot distribution.
families.authentication: Maintainer announced keys for regular API use from 2026-02-13 with limited keyless access. Current quotas/prices require checking at acquisition; no account used.
families.inspected: Creator paper, official blog and dated maintainer access notice inspected; some help pages rendered only shells.
families.reuse_terms: Creator confirms CC0 underlying data and public snapshots. This does not license separately obtained article PDFs or all full text.
limitations: Coauthorship and affiliation do not directly measure coordination or decision authority.
Incomplete abstracts/references and changing disambiguation can shift novelty measures.
A literature graph is neither a verified effect-size database nor evidence that an agent configuration behaves as advertised.
families.suggested_task: Build a dated source-linked entry/recombination measure, explicitly tracing institution and topic definitions.
families.review_decision: Openly licensed graph complement; less immediate than source-level organizational records for a first demonstration.

families.name: AMI Meeting Corpus
families.release: Manual annotations v1.6.2, 2017-04-10 (content unchanged since 2014-06-16); automatic annotations v1.5.1, 2017-04-10.
families.units_and_scope: English meeting recordings and synchronized annotations; approximately two-thirds scenario design meetings and one-third natural meetings.
families.size: About 100 hours; manual annotation ZIP 22 MB; automatic annotations 68 MB. Annotation types/coverage vary by session.
families.coverage_and_dates: Time-aligned word-level transcription, speaker turns and meeting sequences. Scenario projects comprise four meetings with four assigned roles.
families.fields_and_links: Meeting and speaker IDs, timed words, dialogue acts, topics and summaries; audio/video, slides and other meeting artifacts where available.
families.access: public download route; core CC BY 4.0 materials
families.route: Official corpus download selector and annotation archives.
families.authentication: Current annotation page exposes direct downloads; legacy overview describes registration. Current binary download was not tested.
families.inspected: Official overview, licensing notice and exact annotation-version entries inspected.
families.reuse_status: explicit CC BY 4.0 with component scope
families.reuse_terms: Main site licenses signals, transcriptions and some annotations CC BY 4.0. Check add-on annotation terms separately; do not extend that statement to every derived layer.
limitations: There is no AI treatment; scenario meetings are not natural firm decisions.
Public talk does not reveal unspoken intentions, off-meeting work, actual approval powers or latent learning.
Existing dialogue-act labels can assist retrieval but do not validate a new organizational construct.
families.suggested_task: Trace proposal, evaluation, disagreement and recorded decision episodes. Link coding to timestamps, preserve contradictory turns and distinguish assigned roles from exercised authority.
families.review_decision: Starter choice for process-rich material with a small annotation package and explicit core licensing.

families.name: WikiConv
families.entry_point_note: ConvoKit documentation of WikiConv; the creator repository itself is on GitHub.
families.release: Creator corpus reconstructed from Wikipedia dumps dated 2018-07-01; creator repository read-only/archived 2026-09-04. ConvoKit supplies year/language subsets with their own representations.
families.units_and_scope: Wikipedia talk-page conversational actions and reconstructed discussion relationships across English, German, Russian, Chinese and Greek.
families.size: Creator English corpus reports 241,288,668 actions and 90,930,244 conversations under its technical definition. ConvoKit's documented English-2003 example has 140,265 utterances and 91,787 conversations; these are not interchangeable counts.
families.coverage_and_dates: Timestamps, revision/action histories and reply relationships support temporal reconstruction. Final utterance text can include later modifications.
families.fields_and_links: Action/utterance, speaker, conversation, page/revision and reply/parent identifiers; text, time, modification/restoration metadata. ConvoKit's representation must be distinguished from raw actions.
families.access: public archives; mixed CC0 and CC BY-SA 3.0 content
families.route: Creator Figshare/Google Cloud links or documented ConvoKit year subsets.
families.authentication: No research-approval requirement stated; no archive downloaded.
families.inspected: Creator README/license and ConvoKit documentation inspected.
families.reuse_terms: Creator labels the dataset CC0 while individual comments remain CC BY-SA 3.0. Preserve comment attribution/share-alike obligations; ConvoKit software licensing does not replace content terms.
limitations: A technical conversation can contain one user; it is not automatically a collaborative episode.
Volunteer discussion differs from employment-based organizing.
Archival maintenance status, later-edited text and platform norms limit transfer to contemporary human–AI teams.
families.suggested_task: Compare conclusions drawn from final text with those drawn from edits, reverts and reply timing; document how a changed state alters an episode interpretation.
families.review_decision: Useful process source for state reconstruction, with more complicated content reuse and data representation than AMI.

families.name: Noy–Zhang AI productivity experiment replication
families.release: OSF project DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/XD7QW; project metadata last modified 2023-07-21T14:22:07.394749. Public file inventories inspected; file-specific versions matter.
families.units_and_scope: Experiment with 453 college-educated professionals performing writing tasks, linked survey/essay data, external grades and follow-up surveys.
families.size: Final study N=453. OSF inspected inventories contain 12 raw-data files and 11 code files; those are package counts, not the analysis sample for every result.
families.coverage_and_dates: Two tasks, minute-level essay snapshots, self-reported task stages, and two-week/two-month follow-ups described in package README.
families.fields_and_links: Hashed participant IDs, treatment/order/incentive variables, task times, essay text snapshots and word-change counts; grader writing/content/originality judgments and justifications. Merge eligibility and analysis sample must follow the original specification.
families.access: public archive and file metadata; no declared license
families.route: OSF native API/file links; UI rendering was unreliable but public inventories and README were readable.
families.authentication: Project public=true, read permission confirmed; no login used.
families.inspected: README PDF inspected in memory and raw/code directory pagination exhausted; actual data and analysis code not acquired or executed.
families.reuse_terms: OSF native metadata returned node_license=null; no dataset license established by the inspected README. Public file links do not establish a redistribution grant.
limitations: Stata Master.do and a Python analysis component require a later environment/dependency check; fixed paths and the revised grade-cleaning file need inspection.
Minute-level text evolution does not reveal which AI outputs were seen, rejected or selected, nor stopping reasons.
Follow-up AI use is not delayed unaided evaluative capability. Do not import older working-paper N=444 into the final study.
families.suggested_task: Reproduce Figure 1 task-time and grade contrasts from the correct final-paper package. Trace discrepancies to sample, grade cleaning, text truncation, task order, software and specification.
families.review_decision: Promising exact-replication candidate with concrete access evidence; reuse and runtime fidelity remain unresolved.

families.name: Hybrid working from home experiment replication
families.release: Harvard Dataverse replication DOI 10.7910/DVN/6X4ZZL, version 1.1, updated 2024-05-20 according to DataCite registration.
families.units_and_scope: Trip.com hybrid-work randomized experiment and anonymized outcome files described by the Nature article.
families.size: Study N=1,612 workers. Public package file counts, sizes and exact field inventory not verified.
families.coverage_and_dates: Six-month experiment August 2021–January 2022; article reports performance follow-up spanning July 2021–June 2023.
families.fields_and_links: Article describes assignment, attrition, performance reviews, promotion, surveys and a code-output subset. Which fields and joins are exposed in the public package remains to verify.
families.access: explicit CC BY 4.0 metadata; file access unverified
families.route: Harvard Dataverse DOI deposit.
families.authentication: Unknown for files. Dataverse UI/native routes failed or returned 403 in this inspection; DOI metadata was readable.
families.inspected: Nature data-availability statement and DataCite release/rights metadata inspected. No public file inventory or download verified.
families.reuse_terms: DataCite rightsList explicitly identifies CC BY 4.0. File-specific conditions and availability still need to be inspected on the deposit.
limitations: The article says data are split/anonymized to reduce reidentification; do not reconstruct an unrestricted person-level panel across deliberately separated files.
This is not an AI experiment and does not reveal aspirations or internal coordination decisions.
DOI licensing metadata confirms a declared license, not successful acquisition or runnable replication.
families.suggested_task: Reconstruct the reported retention contrast and performance analysis, identifying which anonymized files supply each result.
families.review_decision: Promising explicitly licensed replication candidate; archive file inventory still needs inspection.

families.name: QASPER
families.release: Creator HF revision fdc9d8214fbab5dd782958601db4d678e6934a54, modified 2022-10-07. A repository revision does not pin every external file used by its loader.
families.units_and_scope: Questions and evidence-linked answers about NLP research papers.
families.size: 5,049 questions over 1,585 papers.
families.coverage_and_dates: Fixed benchmark content; no organizational event panel.
families.fields_and_links: Paper IDs, title/abstract, structured full-text paragraphs, questions, answer types, evidence passages and figure/table captions or references. Includes unanswerable and yes/no questions.
families.access: public benchmark; explicit CC BY 4.0
families.route: AllenAI creator HF card/files and paper-linked release.
families.authentication: gated=false in native metadata; no loader executed or data downloaded.
families.inspected: Creator card, native version metadata and paper inspected.
families.reuse_terms: Creator card declares CC BY 4.0. Separate source PDFs/additional article content require their own terms; Apache-2.0 baseline software license is distinct.
limitations: This is a supporting benchmark, not a substantive organizational dataset or validation of organizational constructs.
Well-known public benchmark exposure can confound current-model comparisons.
Evidence-match success does not establish correct downstream inference or genuine scientific discovery.
families.suggested_task: Compare ordinary answering with answer-plus-evidence checking and explicit abstention.
families.review_decision: Compact evidence-grounding fixture to use alongside a substantive source.

families.name: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database — current structured release
families.release: Live daily database; Release 24 (September 2026) removed complaint narratives and visualizations. Release 23 (July 2026) capped filtered CSV exports at 100,000 and retired JSON exports.
families.units_and_scope: Published consumer complaints and structured company-response categories.
families.size: Live population; no current exact row count verified. Download-export limits are not total population counts.
families.coverage_and_dates: Received/sent dates; historical coverage varies by product. Taxonomies and released fields change.
families.fields_and_links: Complaint ID, product/subproduct, issue/subissue, company, received/sent dates, submitted-via channel, state/ZIP and response/timeliness fields. Current public text narratives are absent.
families.access: public structured data; explicit free-use statement
families.route: Official public CSV exports and documented API, subject to current release changes.
families.authentication: Public routes have no account requirement stated; no complaint records acquired.
families.inspected: Current main page, API fields and September-2026 release notes inspected.
families.reuse_terms: Main page states published data are freely available for use, analysis and building on; no standardized CC license was identified. Follow current source and sharing guidance.
limitations: Current acquisition cannot supply the former narrative-text task. Unverified mirrors are not a substitute for the current release.
Published complaints are selected reports with no market-exposure denominator; rates are not population failure probabilities.
Company public responses are preset categories, not free-form conversations; consent/disputed fields also changed in June 2026.
families.suggested_task: Validate date/grouping/timeliness aggregation and show how a pipeline expecting narrative text detects the removed field rather than silently changing its task.
families.review_decision: Retain for structured fields and the source-change example; unsuitable for current narrative-based selection.

families.name: UCI Online Retail
families.release: UCI deposit donated 2015-11-05; DOI 10.24432/C5BW33; named file Online Retail.xlsx. No binary checksum acquired.
families.units_and_scope: Transaction line items from one UK online retailer, including many wholesale customers.
families.size: 541,909 rows; workbook listed as 22.6 MB.
families.coverage_and_dates: 2010-12-01 through 2011-12-09; timestamped invoices.
families.fields_and_links: InvoiceNo, StockCode, Description, Quantity, InvoiceDate, UnitPrice, CustomerID, Country. Invoice numbers beginning with C indicate cancellations; product and customer identifiers permit grouping.
families.access: public-download; explicit CC BY 4.0
families.route: Official UCI workbook download.
families.authentication: No login required by the displayed route; workbook not acquired.
families.inspected: Official creator deposit page inspected, including variables, file and license.
families.reuse_terms: UCI explicitly permits sharing/adaptation with attribution under CC BY 4.0.
limitations: One firm's transactions do not support a multi-firm theory test or customer-exposure denominator.
Repository metadata's missingness claim is not a substitute for profiling the workbook; no data-level completeness was verified.
A deterministic business-data control isolates computation failures but does not establish the validity of text-based organizational measures.
families.suggested_task: Calculate a predeclared sales/return summary and identify how cancellation treatment, missing customer IDs and line-versus-invoice units change the conclusion.
families.review_decision: Lean, explicitly licensed structured control alongside a substantive text task.

families.name: CoAuthor human–AI collaborative writing
families.release: CHI 2022 dataset; primary paper arXiv:2201.06796v2 (2022-01-25). Creator links to Drive session files and Google Sheets metadata/surveys; a versioned binary manifest was not exposed/inspected.
families.units_and_scope: English writing sessions by 63 crowd writers interacting with four instances of GPT-3.
families.size: 1,445 sessions: 830 creative stories and 615 argumentative essays. File bytes not verified.
families.coverage_and_dates: Timestamped interaction/keystroke sequences within sessions. Collection calendar range and cross-session identifiers require release-file verification.
families.fields_and_links: Session events capture writing, cursor movement, requested suggestions, acceptance/dismissal and subsequent edits. Session metadata and surveys are linked from the creator site; exact raw key names/joins remain to inspect.
families.access: public creator download links; dataset reuse unresolved
families.route: Creator Drive files, metadata/survey sheet and session replay interface.
families.authentication: No account requirement stated on the landing page; binary/Sheet access not tested.
families.inspected: Creator overview and primary paper inspected; separate interface repository verified.
families.reuse_terms: No explicit data-specific reuse grant established. The interface is MIT-licensed and the arXiv paper has CC BY 4.0; neither automatically licenses session content, survey data or source prompts. Third-party license labels were not adopted.
limitations: Suggestion display does not prove attention, comprehension or a change in private criteria; session termination does not explain stopping motives.
Crowd writing with 2022-era systems does not establish contemporary workplace coordination, durable skill or multi-agent authority.
Do not silently equate the interface software release with the original dataset or use derivative-repository licenses as source-data permission.
families.suggested_task: Reconstruct candidate→displayed suggestion→accept/dismiss→edit paths and compare them with conclusions from final text alone. Distinguish a recorded interface action from its interpretation.
families.review_decision: High-value writing-process source for interaction diagnostics, conditional on data reuse clarification.

families.name: Doshi–Hauser creativity experiment replication
families.release: Dryad release dated 2024-06-14; DataCite version 6. Related Zenodo record 11654403 reports the same Dryad DOI and CC0. ZIP md5 b329200a3bab35b5326fdd6c7191eaa8.
families.units_and_scope: Randomized short-story writing experiment with separate evaluators and post-disclosure ownership judgments.
families.size: 293 stories/writers; 600 evaluators and 3,519 retained evaluations. Archive lists a 2,472,080-byte scripts/data ZIP and 3,657-byte README.
families.coverage_and_dates: One experimental writing/evaluation sequence; release date is not collection date. No delayed unaided follow-up established.
families.fields_and_links: Conditions: human-only, access to one AI idea, access to up to five ideas; story content, writer assessments, evaluator novelty/usefulness judgments and ownership responses. Exact variable names and story/evaluator merge keys require file inspection.
families.access: public archive; explicit CC0
families.route: Dryad canonical deposit and related Zenodo distribution; README describes raw CSV and processed Stata data.
families.authentication: Public listing/download links, Zenodo access_right=open. No files acquired.
families.inspected: Deposit README rendered in-page; native DataCite and Zenodo metadata checked.
families.reuse_terms: DataCite rightsList and Zenodo metadata explicitly identify CC0 for this deposit. Separate dependencies and software retain their own terms.
limitations: The full rebuild requires Python, external language resources and an OpenAI API key; live calls may not reproduce historical embeddings/results. Processed-data analysis avoids that rebuild but still needs Stata/dependencies.
README mentions GenAI_creativity_data_and_scripts.zip while the listed file is GenAI_creativity_scripts.zip; inspect archive inventory before claiming runnable reproduction.
Creativity ratings are domain-specific judgments. Better rated stories, collective diversity and durable unaided capability are different outcomes.
families.suggested_task: Follow the documented processed-data analysis path first, then separately diagnose which conclusions depend on rebuilding similarity/preprocessing inputs. Reconcile assignment, actual idea use and exclusions.
families.review_decision: Preferred portable replication candidate: explicit license, compact package and two documented reproducibility paths. Execution remains untested.

families.name: BPI Challenge 2017 loan-application event log
families.release: 4TU dataset version 1, issued 2017-02-06; archive item 12696884. Canonical DOI metadata checked; Figshare-hosted record rendered.
families.units_and_scope: Applications, multiple offers per application, and operational workflow events at one Dutch financial institution.
families.size: Archive lists 28.29 MB compressed. A published challenge analysis reports 31,509 applications, 42,995 offers and 149 originators; originators include employees or systems, not necessarily distinct workers.
families.coverage_and_dates: Applications filed during 2016; subsequent events through 2017-02-01 per archive. Timestamp/lifecycle interpretation and end-of-window censoring need checking.
families.fields_and_links: Application and offer IDs; application type, requested amount and loan goal; offer amounts/terms, selected/accepted indicators, credit score and creating employee. Application/offer/workflow event classes permit case trajectories; verify actual XES attribute names and lifecycle fields.
families.access: public archive; custom legacy terms not fully resolved
families.route: 4TU canonical DOI and linked Figshare record, compressed XML/XES distribution.
families.authentication: Public download displayed; no archive acquisition attempted.
families.inspected: Native DOI metadata, deposit description and primary challenge analysis inspected. Legacy DOI/terms resolver and organizer page failed in the browser.
families.reuse_status: 4TU General Terms of Use; operative text unresolved
families.reuse_terms: Deposit and DataCite label the original release with 4TU General Terms of Use. Do not substitute CC BY 4.0 from a later derived event-graph release or Apache/MIT from analysis code. Inspect operative terms before redistribution.
limitations: Elapsed time between events is not hands-on labor; suspend/resume and parallel work can defeat simple subtraction.
Resource IDs do not reveal actual authority, attention, skill or contractual roles; this has no AI treatment.
The 2012 log is a related earlier system, not an interchangeable release; a system change is not automatically exogenous.
families.suggested_task: Construct NEW case-level handoff/rework observations, maintaining application–offer relations. Compare a naive timestamp summary with lifecycle-aware reconstruction.
families.review_decision: Strong operational-process source, with legacy reuse terms unresolved.

families.name: O*NET 31.0 occupation, task and work-activity database
families.release: Production version 31.0, August 2026; prior versions remain in the release archive. Pin 31.0 rather than a mutable current-data endpoint.
families.units_and_scope: Occupation-specific task statements and aggregate ratings, linked to skills, work activities and work context.
families.size: 31.0 lists 18,838 task statements and 165,780 task-rating rows; ratings cover 911 occupations. Occupation-data table has 1,016 rows, which is a different coverage denominator.
families.coverage_and_dates: Release versions and field-update dates; a quarterly release is not a repeated survey of every occupation. Avoid interpreting asynchronous updates as real work change.
families.fields_and_links: O*NET-SOC code + Task ID link statements and ratings; task type, source and update date; ratings include scale/category, value, N, uncertainty and suppression flags. Tasks-to-DWA maps provide a further work-activity join.
families.access: public static downloads; CC BY 4.0
families.route: Official Excel/CSV/JSON, SQL and RDF files with release-specific dictionaries.
families.authentication: Static downloads are public; developer registration is optional. Web Services have a separate sign-up route.
families.inspected: 31.0 release/archive, task dictionaries and license inspected; files not downloaded.
families.reuse_status: CC BY 4.0 for specified downloadable database files
families.reuse_terms: Attribute the database version and USDOL/ETA, link the license and identify modifications. Trademark rules and separate career-exploration-tool licenses still apply; database terms do not license every O*NET website/tool.
limitations: Occupation aggregates are not observed employees, establishments or workflows.
Task descriptions do not establish AI adoption, feasible automation, time saved, authority transfer or job displacement.
A new questionnaire requires respondent testing; reusing O*NET wording does not validate the new instrument.
families.suggested_task: Develop a source-linked coding scheme for information needs, review requirements and possible human/AI allocation. Keep inferred allocation labels separate from official task attributes.
families.review_decision: Portable source for task and instrument design, with an explicit license and detailed versioned dictionaries.

families.name: GLEIF Golden Copy legal entities and relationships
families.release: Live Golden Copy files issued three times daily; schema documentation lists LEI-CDF 3.1, Relationship Record CDF 2.1 and Reporting Exceptions 2.1. No timestamped file release acquired.
families.units_and_scope: LEI-identified legal entities, direct/ultimate accounting-consolidating parent relationships and explicit reporting exceptions.
families.size: Current exact record count/bytes not verified. Choose a dated file manifest or bounded API result in later acquisition.
families.coverage_and_dates: Registration/update information and current relationship records; delta windows of 8 hours, 24 hours, 7 days and 31 days. A database change is not necessarily the date of an ownership event.
families.fields_and_links: LEI links entity reference data and parent/child relationships; legal names, addresses, mapped identifiers where available and exceptions. Missing parent LEI, no parent and non-reporting reasons must remain distinct.
families.access: public, no registration; CC0
families.route: Official Golden Copy/delta files and API; API offers field/name searches and relationship retrieval.
families.authentication: GLEIF documents free access without registration; no data acquired.
families.inspected: Official release/schema, API/access and terms pages inspected.
families.reuse_terms: GLEIF's LEI Data Terms of Use explicitly provide data through the Access Service under CC0. Preserve source/version provenance for research even where attribution is not a license condition.
limitations: Accounting-consolidating parenthood is not all beneficial ownership, voting control or everyday decision authority.
Entities with LEIs are a selected population, not a census of firms.
Current Golden Copy relationships do not supply a full historical ownership panel; examples in schema documentation are not observed validation cases. Do not assume an automatic CIK–LEI bridge.
families.suggested_task: Construct a new adjudicated entity-resolution/parent-reporting table, optionally matched to SEC issuers where a defensible mapping exists. A later change dataset would require historical versions and event-source corroboration.
families.review_decision: Strong legal-entity complement to SEC: explicit CC0, durable identifiers and meaningful missingness categories.

families.name: SocioPatterns contacts in a workplace
families.release: Creator release posted 2016-06-23; two named files on the dataset page. File hashes were not obtained.
families.units_and_scope: Anonymous person-pair proximity/contact intervals and workplace departments in one French office.
families.size: Creator lists 153 KB contact file and 0.8 KB department file. Exact participant/event counts were not independently verified in this round.
families.coverage_and_dates: 2013-06-24 to 2013-07-03; 20-second intervals measured relative to midnight on June 24.
families.fields_and_links: Contact table t,i,j; department table i,Di. Join anonymous person ID i (or j) to department; interval represented as [t−20 seconds,t].
families.access: public direct files; CC0
families.route: Creator tab-separated contact and department files.
families.authentication: Direct downloads shown with no login; no records downloaded.
families.inspected: Creator schema/period/size/terms page and linked CC0 deed inspected.
families.reuse_terms: Creator explicitly links the Creative Commons Public Domain Dedication; requests citation to the associated Network Science paper.
limitations: Co-presence/contact does not reveal speech content, cooperation, information exchange or decision rights.
One short office observation cannot establish enduring organizational structure or an AI effect.
Anonymity does not justify reidentification; department/temporal coverage may be selective. No clinical or vaccination recommendation is proposed.
families.suggested_task: Build an interdepartmental contact-duration network and compare justified temporal aggregation rules. Keep the output labeled recorded contact, not collaboration.
families.review_decision: Small, openly reusable non-text process contrast; useful for construct discipline rather than rich qualitative theory building.

families.name: WildChat writing-interaction annotations (Mysore et al.)
families.entry_point_note: The annotations paper; the creator repository itself is on GitHub.
families.release: Creator repository ID 992823885; pinned commit 65b858edb2be77bca417cafdb06a2c4cb4c113b5, 2025-09-19. Derived from WildChat-1M; do not count the parent as another new family here.
families.units_and_scope: Observed user–LLM conversation sessions with machine-produced task, follow-up and writing-intent labels.
families.size: README lists 159,134 selected sessions, 68,782 writing sessions and 32,697 final analysis sessions after annotation-alignment filtering. These are nested stages, not additive samples.
families.coverage_and_dates: Turn order and conversation timestamp; README specifies timestamp as last turn in UTC, not an event time for every user action.
families.fields_and_links: convid, ordered turns(author,utterance), model and timestamp; coarse_tasks, utterance_types and writing_intents. Repository also includes IP-derived fields; they are unnecessary for the proposed task and should be omitted.
families.access: public creator repository; ODC-BY dataset declaration
families.route: Three documented JSONL-related files in data/ at the pinned commit.
families.authentication: Public GitHub metadata and README readable without login; data files not acquired.
families.inspected: Native repo/commit metadata and exact-commit README inspected; primary paper checked.
families.reuse_terms: README explicitly licenses data ODC-BY. This database-level license should not be treated as clearance for every user-authored utterance; retain upstream provenance and inspect sharing/privacy scope before distributing raw conversations.
limitations: GPT-4o labels are model outputs, not human ground truth. The README's three-utterance selection wording needs reconciliation with the paper/actual records before sampling.
Only public WildChat material is released; do not assume access to every source used in the paper.
README still marks analysis/data-generation code as TODO. Conversation endings do not establish stopping reasons; logs do not show copied text, external editing, attention or actual workplace roles.
families.suggested_task: Recode user requests and revisions using a human-checked event dictionary; compare inferred collaboration patterns before and after correcting labels and selection.
families.review_decision: Observational complement to controlled CoAuthor; labels, filtering and missing analysis code need validation.
